summary.text: A finite recurrence computation for the base values, together with fast-doubling Fibonacci arithmetic modulo \(p=195318521017\), shows that the asserted closed form would make both \(a_{249580077006}\) and \(a_{249580077007}\) divisible by \(p\). Their gcd is therefore greater than \(1\); writing the two positive terms as \(ga,gb\) gives \(g+(ga+gb)/g=g+a+b<1+ga+gb\), contradicting the claimed additive formula at \(n=249580077008\).

full_proof.text:
Let \(F_0=0,F_1=1\), and \(F_{r+2}=F_{r+1}+F_r\). Let \(a(1)=a(2)=1\), and for \(n\geq 3\) put
\[
 a(n)=g+\frac{a(n-1)+a(n-2)}g,
 \qquad g=\gcd(a(n-1),a(n-2)).
\]
All terms of the sequence are positive: this is immediate by induction, since the gcd of two positive integers is positive.

We will show that the first and third asserted formulas in the conjecture are already incompatible. (Thus the second asserted formula is not needed.) The counterexample is obtained indirectly at the index
\[
 N=249{,}580{,}077{,}008.
\]
Set
\[
 M=N-1=249{,}580{,}077{,}007
\]
and introduce the modulus
\[
 P=195{,}318{,}521{,}017.
\]
The role of \(P\) is that, if the conjectured Fibonacci formula held at both \(M-1\) and \(M\), it would force both \(a(M-1)\) and \(a(M)\) to be divisible by \(P\). Their gcd would therefore be at least \(P>1\), making the actual defining recurrence at \(N\) strictly smaller than the conjectured value \(1+a(M)+a(M-1)\).

We first give all the finite computations needed to establish those two divisibilities.

Directly iterating the defining recurrence through index \(3774\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(3772)={}&50{,}821{,}856{,}637{,}385{,}792{,}267{,}808{,}398{,}991{,}468{,}475{,}721{,}843{,}483{,}337{,}998{,}623{,}640{,}757{,}098{,}602{,}636{,}928{,}393{,}269{,}892{,}952{,}934{,}230{,}874{,}475{,}945{,}024{,}513{,}818{,}501{,}434{,}870{,}581{,}449{,}774{,}982{,}213{,}886{,}818{,}298{,}525{,}314{,}166{,}884{,}933{,}137{,}805{,}368{,}884{,}278{,}748{,}201{,}859{,}762{,}766{,}881{,}515{,}372{,}183{,}084{,}024{,}083{,}577{,}995{,}511{,}024{,}802{,}455{,}180{,}968{,}712{,}692{,}288{,}879{,}507{,}888{,}937{,}250{,}291{,}063{,}504{,}680{,}754{,}992{,}157{,}949{,}256{,}964{,}474{,}278{,}019{,}411{,}768{,}646{,}907{,}989{,}461{,}240{,}384{,}266{,}638{,}096{,}191{,}096{,}905{,}619{,}665,
\\[2mm]
a(3774)={}&58{,}247{,}620{,}166{,}949{,}433{,}924{,}152{,}349{,}110{,}387{,}952{,}083{,}697{,}979{,}943{,}894{,}432{,}862{,}563{,}828{,}976{,}040{,}095{,}229{,}520{,}447{,}551{,}846{,}447{,}106{,}151{,}838{,}744{,}759{,}854{,}302{,}693{,}877{,}131{,}497{,}631{,}690{,}251{,}007{,}647{,}345{,}990{,}824{,}945{,}923{,}089{,}962{,}629{,}840{,}263{,}458{,}365{,}713{,}419{,}764{,}969{,}401{,}061{,}223{,}771{,}086{,}474{,}022{,}889{,}794{,}898{,}006{,}618{,}157{,}003{,}102{,}858{,}034{,}604{,}369{,}810{,}330{,}403{,}334{,}719{,}184{,}536{,}749{,}507{,}414{,}607{,}510{,}201{,}847{,}709{,}900{,}422{,}830{,}948{,}846{,}697{,}746{,}280{,}327{,}160{,}364{,}518{,}807{,}058{,}513{,}260{,}008{,}283.
\end{aligned}
\]
For clarity, this finite recurrence computation can be reproduced without storing all preceding terms as follows. Start with \((u,v)=(1,1)\). For \(j=3,4,\ldots,3774\), compute
\[
 g=\gcd(u,v),\qquad w=g+\frac{u+v}{g},
\]
and replace \((u,v)\) by \((v,w)\). At stage \(j\), the new \(v\) is \(a(j)\). Reducing the displayed outputs modulo \(P\) gives the only facts about these terms that will be needed:
\[
 a(3772)\equiv21{,}827{,}756{,}562\pmod P,
 \qquad
 a(3774)\equiv99{,}768{,}150{,}821\pmod P.
\]
Consequently, if
\[
 C=a(3774)+1,\qquad D=a(3772)+1,
\]
then
\[
 C\equiv99{,}768{,}150{,}822\pmod P,
 \qquad
 D\equiv21{,}827{,}756{,}563\pmod P. \tag{1}
\]

We next need four Fibonacci residues at very large indices. They are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 r&F_r\pmod P\\ \hline
249{,}580{,}073{,}235&161{,}033{,}639{,}884\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}234&139{,}205{,}883{,}321\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}233&21{,}827{,}756{,}563\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}232&117{,}378{,}126{,}758.
\end{array} \tag{2}
\]
Here is a reproducible fast-doubling computation of this table. If a pair \((A,B)\) represents \((F_q,F_{q+1})\) modulo \(P\), define
\[
 E=A(2B-A)\pmod P,
 \qquad
 O=A^2+B^2\pmod P.
\]
The standard Fibonacci doubling identities
\[
 F_{2q}=F_q(2F_{q+1}-F_q),
 \qquad
 F_{2q+1}=F_q^2+F_{q+1}^2
\]
show that \((E,O)\) represents \((F_{2q},F_{2q+1})\). Therefore, on reading a binary digit \(b\), replace
\[
 (A,B)\longmapsto
 \begin{cases}
 (E,O),&b=0,\\
 (O,E+O),&b=1,
 \end{cases}
 \pmod P.
\]
Starting from \((A,B)=(0,1)=(F_0,F_1)\) and reading the binary expansion from left to right gives \((F_r,F_{r+1})\) at the end. The four binary strings used here are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
249{,}580{,}073{,}235&11101000011100001000011011000100010011\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}234&11101000011100001000011011000100010010\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}233&11101000011100001000011011000100010001\\
249{,}580{,}073{,}232&11101000011100001000011011000100010000.
\end{array}
\]
Applying the displayed two modular multiplications at each bit gives exactly the residues in (2). The doubling identities also prove inductively that this finite computation calculates the claimed Fibonacci residues.

Now suppose, for contradiction, that all three formulas in the conjecture hold for every \(n\geq3775\). In particular, its third formula says
\[
 a(n)=C F_{n-3772}-D F_{n-3774}-1. \tag{3}
\]
Apply (3) first at \(n=M\). The two Fibonacci indices are
\[
 M-3772=249{,}580{,}073{,}235,
 \qquad
 M-3774=249{,}580{,}073{,}233.
\]
Using (1) and (2), the right side of (3), modulo \(P\), is
\[
 99{,}768{,}150{,}822\cdot161{,}033{,}639{,}884
 -21{,}827{,}756{,}563\cdot21{,}827{,}756{,}563-1.
\]
The two products, before reduction, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
99{,}768{,}150{,}822\cdot161{,}033{,}639{,}884
 &=16{,}066{,}028{,}471{,}362{,}546{,}584{,}648,\\
21{,}827{,}756{,}563^2
 &=476{,}450{,}956{,}573{,}589{,}572{,}969.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their difference minus one is
\[
15{,}589{,}577{,}514{,}788{,}957{,}011{,}678
 =79{,}816{,}176{,}334\,P.
\]
Thus
\[
 P\mid a(M). \tag{4}
\]

Apply (3) next at \(n=M-1\). This time
\[
 (M-1)-3772=249{,}580{,}073{,}234,
 \qquad
 (M-1)-3774=249{,}580{,}073{,}232.
\]
The corresponding modular calculation is
\[
 99{,}768{,}150{,}822\cdot139{,}205{,}883{,}321
 -21{,}827{,}756{,}563\cdot117{,}378{,}126{,}758-1.
\]
Here
\[
\begin{aligned}
99{,}768{,}150{,}822\cdot139{,}205{,}883{,}321
 &=13{,}888{,}313{,}562{,}479{,}262{,}239{,}862,\\
21{,}827{,}756{,}563\cdot117{,}378{,}126{,}758
 &=2{,}562{,}101{,}176{,}694{,}580{,}412{,}754,
\end{aligned}
\]
and hence their difference minus one is
\[
11{,}326{,}212{,}385{,}784{,}681{,}827{,}107
 =57{,}988{,}419{,}771\,P.
\]
Therefore
\[
 P\mid a(M-1). \tag{5}
\]

There is no issue here concerning subtraction if the formula is interpreted over the integers: under the assumed equality, its right side equals the positive integer \(a(n)\). If instead each subtraction in the displayed OEIS formula is interpreted as truncated subtraction on nonnegative integers, the same conclusion still follows. Indeed, write the expression as \(X-Y-1\). If \(X\geq Y+1\), reduction modulo \(P\) agrees with ordinary integer subtraction. If \(X<Y+1\), the truncated value is zero, which is also divisible by \(P\). Thus the modular conclusions (4) and (5) are valid under either convention.

Set
\[
 x=a(M),\qquad y=a(M-1),\qquad g=\gcd(x,y).
\]
Both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive. By (4) and (5), \(P\) is a common divisor of \(x\) and \(y\), so
\[
 P\mid g.
\]
In particular, since \(P>1\),
\[
 g\geq P\geq2. \tag{6}
\]
Because \(g\) divides both \(x\) and \(y\), write
\[
 x=gu,
 \qquad
 y=gv
\]
for positive integers \(u,v\). Thus \(s=u+v\geq2\). The defining recurrence at \(N=M+1\) gives
\[
 a(N)=g+\frac{x+y}{g}=g+u+v=g+s. \tag{7}
\]
On the other hand, the first formula in the conjecture, applied at the same index \(N\), gives
\[
 a(N)=1+a(N-1)+a(N-2)=1+x+y=1+g(u+v)=1+gs. \tag{8}
\]
But (6) and \(s\geq2\) imply
\[
 g+s\leq gs<1+gs.
\]
For the first inequality, one may rewrite it as
\[
 gs-g-s=(g-1)(s-1)-1\geq0,
\]
since both \(g-1\) and \(s-1\) are at least \(1\). The second inequality is strict for every integer \(gs\). Thus (7) and (8) assign two unequal values to \(a(N)\), a contradiction.

All three indices used, \(M-1\), \(M\), and \(N\), are much larger than \(3775\), so the assumed universal range condition applies to each of them. Hence it is false that the three claimed formulas hold for every \(n\geq3775\), and the stated conjecture is disproved.
